title: Flat Hom-complex model for a target of finite relative Tor dimension
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Work in ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived scalar extension [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data] and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Let $K,L\in D(S)$, assume $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $S$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and suppose that for some integers $a\le b$, every $R$-module $N$ satisfies $H^j(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$. There exist a bounded-above cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $S$-modules representing $K$ and a bounded cochain complex $F^\bullet$ of $S$-modules representing $L$ whose terms are flat over $R$ (tensoring with each term preserves exact sequences). Cochain complexes use [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], on the one-object site. For any such $P,F$, put $E^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,F)$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], so $E^n=\bigoplus_p\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^p,F^{p+n})$ (only finitely many summands are nonzero) and $d(h)=d_Fh-(-1)^nhd_P$. The complex $E$ is bounded below with $R$-flat terms and represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(K,L)$ in $D(S)$. For every homomorphism $R\to T$ of commutative rings, put $S_T=S\otimes_RT$, $K_T=K\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S_T$ and $L_T=L\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S_T$. The ordinary termwise tensors $P\otimes_RT$ and $F\otimes_RT$ represent $K_T$ and $L_T$, and the chain isomorphism
$$E\otimes_RT\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}^\bullet(P\otimes_RT,F\otimes_RT),\qquad (h\otimes t)(p\otimes u)=h(p)\otimes tu$$
induces an isomorphism $E\otimes_RT\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}(K_T,L_T)$ in $D(S_T)$. In particular it gives an additive isomorphism $H^0(E\otimes_RT)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S_T)}(K_T,L_T)$. For every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $T\to U$, the cohomology map of the chain map $E\otimes_RT\to E\otimes_RU$, $h\otimes t\mapsto h\otimes\overline t$, corresponds under these isomorphisms to derived scalar extension from $S_T$ to $S_U$ (using the canonical iterated-tensor identifications of $K_T,L_T$ with $K_U,L_U$ after extension). The comparisons respect identities and composition of $T\to U$. No finite-presentation assumption on $R\to S$, no pseudo-coherence assumption on $L$, and no flatness assumption on $R\to T$ or $T\to U$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose $P$ from the definition of pseudo-coherence. Taking $N=R$ in the hypothesis shows that $H^j(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-above-projective-model] over $S$ to obtain a projective complex $Q$ representing $L$, zero above $b$. Its terms are $S$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], hence $R$-flat by [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive]. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], $Q$ computes $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ by ordinary tensor for every $N$. Its tensor cohomology in degree $a-1$ therefore vanishes universally. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] over $R$: $Q^a/\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{a-1})$ is $R$-flat. Define $F^i=0$ for $i<a$, $F^a=Q^a/\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{a-1})$, and $F^i=Q^i$ for $i>a$, with the induced differential. The quotient chain map $Q\to F$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees $i\ge a$; below $a$ both cohomologies vanish. Thus $F$ represents $L$ and is supported in $[a,b]$, with all terms $R$-flat. Projective terms suffice in this construction; no finite-generation condition on $Q$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, first proof paragraph; Tag 0653, lemma-last-one-flat; projective replacement from derived.tex Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist

proof.text: Now take any $P,F$ allowed by the statement, with $P^p=0$ for $p>m$ and $F^q=0$ outside $[c,d]$. In degree $n$ the product defining [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] has nonzero factors only for $c-n\le p\le\min(m,d-n)$, a finite interval. It is therefore the displayed finite direct sum, and vanishes for $n<c-m$. Choose a finite basis of each $P^p$, of rank $r_p$; then $\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^p,F^{p+n})\cong(F^{p+n})^{r_p}$. Hence each $E^n$ is a finite product of $R$-flat modules, flat by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules], including empty products. Finite free modules are projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and $F$ is bounded, in particular bounded below. Hence [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], applied over $S$ to the bounded-above projective complex $P$ and the bounded-below complex $F$, says that $E=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,F)$ represents the derived Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site with ring $S$; since $P,F$ represent $K,L$, this is the derived-category isomorphism $Q_SE\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_S(K,L)$.

For arbitrary $R\to T$, both $P$ and $F$ are bounded-above $R$-flat complexes: for $P$ use [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] and [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive], and for $F$ use its hypothesis. They are $R$-K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. For either complex $C$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-derived-module-tensor-exchange] with $N=T$ and an augmented free $R$-resolution $V\to T[0]$. It identifies $Q_S\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_RV)$ with $Q_SC\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S_T$ and identifies the derived-to-ordinary comparison with $1_C\otimes(V\to T[0])$. This augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism: its cone is $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R\operatorname{Cone}(V\to T[0]))$, up to the usual tensor-cone signs, and is acyclic by $R$-K-flatness of $C$. Consequently $C\otimes_RT$ represents the required derived scalar extension, with its $S_T$-action. In particular $P_T=P\otimes_RT$ and $F_T=F\otimes_RT$ represent $K_T,L_T$. The terms $P_T^p\cong S_T^{r_p}$ are finite free, and $F_T$ remains bounded.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, proof of (b), first paragraph; Tag 0661, lemma-base-change-comparison

proof.text: The termwise map $\beta_T$ sends $h\otimes t$ to $(p\otimes u\mapsto h(p)\otimes tu)$. For $P^p=S^{r_p}$ its degree-$(p,p+n)$ component is the coordinate isomorphism $(F^{p+n})^{r_p}\otimes_RT\cong(F^{p+n}\otimes_RT)^{r_p}$: a tuple supported in coordinate $j$, tensored with $t$, maps to the same coordinate tensored with $t$, and the inverse adds these coordinate inclusions. There are finitely many $p$ in each degree by step 2. Distributing tensor over this finite direct sum therefore gives an isomorphism in each degree. Evaluate both differentials on $p\otimes u$: both give $d_Fh(p)\otimes tu-(-1)^nh(d_Pp)\otimes tu$. Thus the degreewise isomorphisms form the stated chain isomorphism. The finite free terms of $P_T$ are projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] and $F_T$ is bounded, in particular bounded below, so [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom] applies over $S_T$ to $P_T,F_T$; together with step 3 this identifies its target with $R\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}(K_T,L_T)$ in $D(S_T)$.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, proof of (b), displayed Hom-complex equality and final sentence

proof.text: The differential on $\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}^\bullet(P_T,F_T)$ makes its degree-zero cycles exactly the chain maps $P_T\to F_T$. A degree-zero boundary is $d_Fs+sd_P$ for a degree-minus-one family $s$, exactly a null-homotopic chain map. Its $H^0$ is consequently the additive group of chain maps modulo homotopy. The bounded-above projective complex $P_T$ is K-projective by [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective]. Apply [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] in $\operatorname{Mod}(S_T)$: localization identifies those homotopy classes with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S_T)}(K_T,L_T)$. All maps here preserve addition (localization is additive and the quotient uses the additive homotopy relation), so this is the asserted additive isomorphism after $\beta_T$.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective, proof, and derived.tex Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex; degree-zero consequence of the Hom-complex model

proof.text: Let $v:T\to U$ be any $R$-algebra map. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], $S_T$ is flat over $T$ and every $F_T^q$ is $T$-flat. The $P_T^p$ are $T$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] and [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive]. They remain bounded above, and $F_T$ remains bounded. Thus step 3, now for $T\to S_T$ and $T\to U$, computes derived scalar extension on both $P_T,F_T$ by ordinary tensor. The balancing identifications are $(P\otimes_RT)\otimes_TU\cong P\otimes_RU$ and the analogous ones for $F$, sending $(x\otimes t)\otimes u$ to $x\otimes v(t)u$. For an elementary homogeneous cochain $h\otimes t$, its image under the chain map of the question, followed by $\beta_U$, takes $p\otimes u$ to $h(p)\otimes v(t)u$. Extending $\beta_T(h\otimes t)$ by scalars gives exactly the same formula. Additivity proves equality for every cochain, in particular every degree-zero cycle. Tensor sends a homotopy $s$ to $s\otimes1$ and preserves $f-g=ds+sd$, so the equality passes to homotopy classes. By step 5 it says exactly that the cohomology map is derived scalar extension on morphisms. For $T\xrightarrow{v}U\xrightarrow{w}W$, both iterated formulas send $h\otimes t$ to $h\otimes w(v(t))$; for the identity they fix it. This proves the identity and composition clauses, with the displayed balancing maps giving the canonical iterated-tensor identifications.
